A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C-JEPA work and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Existing content can be matched despite the title change, appendix renumbering, and layout shifts.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLEVRER question-answering results, Push-T planning results and timings, and masking and auxiliary-conditioning ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds PHYRE rollout and attention case studies in Section 5.3 and Appendix J.

M1.justification: The frozen object encoder, identity-anchor masking, bidirectional predictor, joint history/future objective, auxiliary conditioning, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Recasting masking as control of observability does not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds qualitative evaluation on PHYRE scenes involving gravity, momentum transfer, and multi-body collisions. This provides a limited extension beyond the retained CLEVRER reasoning and Push-T control coverage, rather than a new quantitative benchmark evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the CLEVRER and Push-T experiments, including reconstruction variants and DINO-WM variants. The PHYRE study extends the existing C-JEPA versus OC-JEPA comparison to another dataset; it introduces no new comparator.

E3.justification: The added PHYRE study introduces qualitative assessment through ground-truth versus imagined trajectories and cross-slot attention as an interaction proxy. Existing splits, metrics, training budgets, and MPC settings remain unchanged; both versions already evaluate CLEVRER on the held-out validation set.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix J add two illustrated PHYRE rollout cases and an attention comparison examining physical plausibility and reliance on relevant objects. Existing masking-budget, masking-strategy, reconstruction, and auxiliary-conditioning ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report planning-time averages across three seeds and the same fixed-seed information in Appendix H. v2 adds no repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and A2–A5 and the existing Figure 3 results are unchanged; for example, Push-T success remains 88.67% for C-JEPA and 91.33% for DINO-WM. New PHYRE examples show more plausible C-JEPA rollouts and more concentrated attention to relevant slots than OC-JEPA, adding qualitative findings without revising existing benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, four assumptions, lemma, theorem, corollary statement, and proofs are retained. v1 Appendices L.1–L.2 correspond to v2 M.1 and M.4. New M.2–M.3 paragraphs provide interpretation and shortcut explanations, not new formal results or corrected derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies its theoretical contribution from a causal inductive bias via latent interventions to a useful bias from controlling observability, bringing headline claims closer to qualifications already present in v1 Appendix B. The central method contribution and claims of roughly 20-point counterfactual gains and compact, efficient planning remain.

C2.justification: Appendix J interprets PHYRE rollouts and attention as evidence of interaction-aware prediction and explicitly excludes causal-graph identification. Appendix M.2 adds conditions under which predictive neighborhoods may align with physical interactions. General cautions about confounding and causal identifiability already appeared in v1 Appendix B.

D1.justification: Figure A3 adds a specific repository location for PHYRE visualizations, while Appendix C.1 removes the public evaluation-server link. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and main code-access information is retained. PHYRE-specific training and sampling details are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bakhtin et al. (2019) for PHYRE and connects the new attention analysis to the already cited SPARTAN work. The Push-T citation changes from Bekris et al. to Chi et al. for the same Diffusion Policy paper, constituting a bibliographic correction rather than a different cited work.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Latent Interventions' to 'Latent Masking,' with selective abstract and explanatory revisions and updated author/publication information. Section 5.3, Appendix J, and two explanatory theory subsections are added; subsequent appendices are renumbered. Most existing prose and organization remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures A3 and A4 for PHYRE rollout sequences and attention maps. Tables A4–A5 move later in the appendix, Figure 2's caption changes terminology, and text reflows. Existing illustrations, plots, and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the headline causal framing more consistent with the observability-based qualifications already present in v1 and adds inspectable PHYRE examples supporting the proposed mechanism. These improve clarity and empirical illustration modestly. The gain is limited because the new evidence is qualitative, lacks PHYRE-specific training and sampling details, and leaves the quantitative results and formal analysis unchanged.
